summary: Dependency-confusion beacon exfiltrates host identifiers to hardcoded bare-IP endpoint on install and import
details: The package is a stub shim with no advertised functionality. Its postinstall script and the top-level `main` both invoke `beacon.cjs`, which POSTs the package name, `os.hostname()`, `__dirname` install path, `process.cwd()`, and `process.version` to a hardcoded plain-HTTP bare-IP endpoint at http://185.158.107.175:8787/_ah/dc. `index.js` exports a Proxy that returns no-op functions for any property access, so the host build keeps running while the beacon fires on both `npm install` (postinstall lifecycle) and on any `require()` of the package. The scope `@ppa-web-components` combined with the self-described 'Compatibility shim.' metadata, the absence of real code, and the hardcoded bare-IP reconnaissance endpoint are consistent with a dependency-confusion / typosquat probe designed to confirm successful resolution of an internal package name in a victim build environment and to collect host identifiers that identify the compromised network.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
